+Accepted values are `1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `on`/`off`, `yes`/`no`, and
+`enabled`/`disabled`. With the flag off, no dialog renders, no onboarding state
+is written, and Settings hides the replay action.
+
+### Guidance, not gates
+
+The setup conversation is a nudge, never a prerequisite. If you skip it, the
+home stage keeps a dashed **Tell me what you're building** pill; it reopens the
+conversation exactly where you left off. `/start` and Settings do the same. The conversation also understands a
+natural reply: say "skip", "not now", or "show me the landscape" and it reacts
+instead of recording it as an answer. When a brief exists, it opens on a review
+and asks what changed rather than asking everything again.
+
+### Without a model
+
+When the LLM is unreachable the Studio keeps working:
+
+- A **Working by hand** strip explains the state and offers capture, job map,
+  and context.
+- Messages still return deterministic ODI guidance from the sidecar, labelled
+  **Local guidance**.

+  outcomes recorded, re-scored, and removed. All of it goes through the same
+  local repository the model uses.

+
+The user's context is sent with every chat request, so the assistant starts from
+the product, audience, job, and problem rather than asking for them again.
+
+### The thread is the room
+
+Capture, scoring, simulation, and decisions are conversations. The storefront
+never asks the PM to leave the thread to do work: the agent asks for the
+customer's words or the bet in plain language, then renders the surface that
+carries it. A lens exists for reading and for people who prefer a click, not for
+doing the work.
+
+That is also enforced in the agent's system prompt: it is told to keep every
+artifact in the conversation, never to send the PM to a panel, and to end each
+reply with the next move as an action on the surface.

+## Rich responses
+
+The copilot does not only talk. When a surface carries the evidence better than a
+paragraph, the agent renders one **inline in the conversation**: a scored
+outcome, a ranked opportunity board, a before/after simulation of a bet, a
+customer quote with its lineage, the eight-stage job map, or a decision record.
+Three properties keep this safe and cheap to extend:
+
+- **The catalog is closed and owned by the SPA.**
+  `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` declares nine primitives and six cards, their
+  JSON Schema props, and the description the model reads. There is no HTML, no
+  eval, and no third-party component in the path. Prose is rendered by the same
+  `Markdown` component the transcript already used.
+- **The sidecar is catalog-agnostic.** The SPA sends the catalog with each turn;
+  the sidecar derives the `render_ui` tool schema from it, validates what comes
+  back, and streams a `ui` SSE event. Invalid props return to the model as a tool
+  result naming the exact violation, and the loop offers the tool again, so a
+  fumbled prop is corrected in the same reply. A client that sends no catalog
+  never sees the tool.
+- **Cards are views, never actors.** Every button is an `intent` string that the
+  agent receives as the user's next message — one authority, one audit trail.
+
+A surface is one node tree, streamed as one event:
+
+```json
+{
+  "type": "outcome-card",
+  "props": {
+    "id": "O-1",
+    "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments",
+    "importance": 9,
+    "satisfaction": 3
+  }

+```

+The conversation keeps the order the agent produced: a `delta` appends to the
+open prose part, a `ui` event opens a card, and the next `delta` opens a new
+paragraph after it. The opportunity score is computed from importance and
+satisfaction when the agent omits it, so the ODI formula has exactly one home

+that fails validation is dropped whole, and the surrounding prose still reads.

+# Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend
+
+To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a
+local LLM backend that:
+
+- Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example,
+  `/v1/chat/completions`), and
+- Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**.
+
+A simple fully local option is
+[`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run
+a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server.
+
+## 1. Install a local LLM server
+
+Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for
+platform-specific build notes):
+
+```bash
+pip install llama-cpp-python
+```
+
+## 2. Download a small tools-capable model
+
+Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a
+7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g.
+`C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`.
+
+## 3. Start the OpenAI-compatible server
+
+Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default
+used by the Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat:
+
+```bash
+python -m llama_cpp.server \
+  --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \
+  --model_alias local-tools-model \
+  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \
+  --chat_format openai
+```
+
+This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`.
+
+## 4. Configure the Studio
+
+The Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat read the following environment
+variables (with sensible defaults):
+
+| Variable | Default |
+|---|---|
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` |
+
+You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Living Studio's
+**Settings** panel.
+
+## 5. Verify tool-calling against the MCP server
+
+- (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable:
+
+  ```bash
+  curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models
+  ```
+
+  If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before
+  debugging the MCP client/server.
+
+- Start the MCP server and Studio (via `python scripts/dev.py` or one of the
+  [run modes](living-studio.md)).
+- In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for
+  example: *"Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI
+  repository."*
+- You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for
+  example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI
+  guidance, confirming the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work
+  together.
+- If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI shows a clear error
+  banner indicating the configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with
+  details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps
+  above to fix your local LLM setup.

+# Superpowers (Pi, OpenCode & Freebuff)
+
+This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a
+[Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with
+this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded.
+
+## Enable with Pi
+
+1. Install Pi: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh`
+2. Trust the project (first time only): `pi config --local --approve`
+3. Start Pi: `pi`
+
+The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. Pi clones it and loads:
+
+- **Extension**: `superpowers.ts` — injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at
+  session startup and after compaction
+- **Skills**: 12 Superpowers skills (TDD, subagent-driven-development,
+  systematic-debugging, etc.)
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Superpowers is also available for OpenCode via the plugin in `opencode.json`.
+> The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode
+> compatibility layer.
+
+## Freebuff
+
+This project ships [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) for
+[Freebuff](https://freebuff.com) as repo-local skills plus a session-start
+bootstrap. No plugin or hook is required:
+
+- **Skills**: `.agents/skills/` contains 15 Superpowers skills. Freebuff
+  discovers them automatically; load one with the `skill` tool.
+- **Bootstrap**: `AGENTS.md` injects the `using-superpowers` rules and the
+  Freebuff tool mapping at session start.
+- **Mapping**: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md`
+  maps skill actions to Freebuff tools.
+
+Start Freebuff in the repository and ask "What are your superpowers?" to verify.
+See [docs/superpowers/freebuff-setup.md](superpowers/freebuff-setup.md) for
+update and troubleshooting notes.

+"""Ready-to-use MCP connector presets for common ODI workflows.
+
+Each preset captures everything needed to register a connector for a well-known
+MCP server: the endpoint, how it authenticates, and where its documentation
+lives. Presets are grouped by the five capability areas an outcome-driven
+innovation process needs, so a new workspace can be wired up with
+``agentic-odi connectors add mcp --preset <id>`` instead of hunting for URLs.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import ConnectorConfig
+
+CapabilityArea = Literal[
+    "voice-of-customer",
+    "quantitative-data",
+    "market-intelligence",
+    "strategy-alignment",
+    "knowledge-output",
+]
+
+AREA_LABELS: dict[CapabilityArea, str] = {
+    "voice-of-customer": "Voice of customer & qualitative research",
+    "quantitative-data": "Quantitative data & opportunity scoring",
+    "market-intelligence": "Market & competitive intelligence",
+    "strategy-alignment": "Product strategy & backlog alignment",
+    "knowledge-output": "Strategy & knowledge management output",
+}
+
+ENV_VAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")
+
+
+class UnknownPresetError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, preset_id: str) -> None:
+        self.preset_id = preset_id
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown preset: {preset_id} (try 'agentic-odi connectors catalog')")
+
+
+class UnknownAreaError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, area: str) -> None:
+        self.area = area
+        valid = ", ".join(AREA_LABELS)
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown capability area: {area} (expected one of: {valid})")
+
+
+class ConnectorPreset(BaseModel):
+    """A known MCP server plus the credentials it needs."""
+
+    id: str
+    label: str
+    area: CapabilityArea
+    summary: str
+    url: str
+    auth: Literal["none", "oauth"] = "none"
+    env_vars: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    headers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    docs: str
+    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    is_recommended: bool = False
+
+    def referenced_env_vars(self) -> set[str]:
+        """Environment variables the URL or headers interpolate with ``${VAR}``."""
+        found: set[str] = set()
+        for value in [self.url, *self.headers.values()]:
+            found.update(ENV_VAR_PATTERN.findall(value))
+        return found
+
+
+PRESETS: tuple[ConnectorPreset, ...] = (
+    # 1. Voice of customer & qualitative research
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="notion",
+        label="Notion",
+        is_recommended=True,
+        area="voice-of-customer",

+    # 4. Product strategy & backlog alignment
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="linear",

+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="github",
+        label="GitHub",
+        is_recommended=True,

+        url="https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/",

+        docs=(
+            "https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/customizing-copilot/"
+            "using-model-context-protocol/extending-copilot-chat-with-mcp"
+        ),
+    ),
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="jira",
+        label="Atlassian Jira",
+        area="strategy-alignment",
+        summary="Epics and issues to align delivery work with desired outcomes.",
+        url="https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://www.atlassian.com/platform/remote-mcp-server",
+    ),
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="miro",
+        label="Miro",
+        area="strategy-alignment",
+        summary="Outcome matrices and customer journey maps on a shared board.",
+        url="https://mcp.miro.com/",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://developers.miro.com/docs/miro-mcp",
+    ),
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="figma",
+        label="Figma",
+        area="strategy-alignment",
+        summary="FigJam maps and design context for outcome workshops.",
+        url="https://mcp.figma.com/mcp",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/",
+    ),
+    # 5. Strategy & knowledge management output
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="slack",
+        label="Slack",
+        area="knowledge-output",
+        summary="Post opportunity-score digests and JTBD insights to channels.",
+        url="https://mcp.slack.com/mcp",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://docs.slack.dev/ai/",
+    ),
+)
+
+
+def list_presets(area: str | None = None, recommended: bool = False) -> list[ConnectorPreset]:
+    """Return presets, optionally filtered by capability area or recommendation."""
+    presets = list(PRESETS)
+    if area is not None:
+        if area not in AREA_LABELS:
+            raise UnknownAreaError(area)
+        presets = [preset for preset in presets if preset.area == area]
+    if recommended:
+        presets = [preset for preset in presets if preset.is_recommended]
+    return presets
+
+
+def get_preset(preset_id: str) -> ConnectorPreset:
+    for preset in PRESETS:
+        if preset.id == preset_id:
+            return preset
+    raise UnknownPresetError(preset_id)
+
+
+def connector_config_from_preset(
+    preset: ConnectorPreset,
+    *,
+    name: str | None = None,
+    url: str | None = None,
+    tools: list[str] | None = None,
+    enabled: bool = True,
+) -> ConnectorConfig:
+    """Build a registry entry from a preset, allowing local overrides."""
+    settings: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "url": url or preset.url,
+        "auth": preset.auth,
+        "headers": dict(preset.headers),
+        "env_vars": list(preset.env_vars),
+        "tools": list(tools if tools is not None else preset.tools),
+    }
+    return ConnectorConfig(
+        name=name or preset.id,
+        kind="mcp",
+        enabled=enabled,
+        settings=settings,
+    )
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "AREA_LABELS",
+    "ENV_VAR_PATTERN",
+    "PRESETS",
+    "CapabilityArea",
+    "ConnectorPreset",
+    "UnknownAreaError",
+    "UnknownPresetError",
+    "connector_config_from_preset",
+    "get_preset",
+    "list_presets",
+]

@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+"""Kind registry that maps connector configs onto Connector implementations."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.mcp.connector import MCPClientConnector
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import (
+    ConnectorConfig,
+    McpConnectorSettings,
+    RestConnectorSettings,
+)
+from agentic_odi_connectors.protocol import Connector
+from agentic_odi_connectors.registry import UnknownConnectorKindError
+from agentic_odi_connectors.rest.connector import RestConnector, WebhookConnector
+
+Builder = Callable[[ConnectorConfig], Connector]
+
+_builders: dict[str, Builder] = {}
+
+
+def register_kind(kind: str, builder: Builder) -> None:
+    """Register a builder for a connector kind (mcp today; others later)."""
+    _builders[kind] = builder
+
+
+def known_kinds() -> set[str]:
+    return set(_builders)
+
+
+def build_connector(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
+    try:
+        builder = _builders[config.kind]
+    except KeyError:
+        raise UnknownConnectorKindError(config.kind) from None
+    return builder(config)
+
+
+def _build_mcp(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
+    settings = McpConnectorSettings.model_validate(config.settings)
+    return MCPClientConnector(name=config.name, settings=settings)
+
+
+def _build_rest(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
+    settings = RestConnectorSettings.model_validate(config.settings)
+    return RestConnector(name=config.name, settings=settings)
+
+
+def _build_webhook(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
+    settings = RestConnectorSettings.model_validate(config.settings)
+    return WebhookConnector(name=config.name, settings=settings, kind="webhook")
+
+
+register_kind("mcp", _build_mcp)
+register_kind("rest", _build_rest)
+register_kind("webhook", _build_webhook)

+"""Map connector ingest records onto ODI evidence drafts.
+
+This module deliberately does not import the ODI store. It produces transport
+records shaped for ``core.Evidence``; the CLI (or any caller) owns persistence,
+so connector plumbing never leaks into the ODI repository.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+

+    """An ingest record ready to become ODI evidence."""
+

+    source_kind: str
+    item_type: EvidenceItemType
+    name: str
+    content: str
+    raw: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    job_id: str | None = None
+    step_id: str | None = None
+    outcome_id: str | None = None
+
+
+def drafts_from_batch(
+    batch: IngestBatch,
+    *,
+    job_id: str | None = None,
+    step_id: str | None = None,
+    outcome_id: str | None = None,
+    include_catalog: bool = False,
+) -> list[EvidenceDraft]:
+    """Turn every evidence-bearing record in ``batch`` into a draft.
+
+    Catalog records describe the connector itself and are skipped unless
+    ``include_catalog`` is set.
+    """
+    drafts: list[EvidenceDraft] = []
+    for record in batch.records:
+        if record.item_type == "catalog" and not include_catalog:
+            continue

+def _draft_from_record(

+    job_id: str | None,

+    return EvidenceDraft(

+        source_kind=record.source_kind,
+        item_type=record.item_type,
+        name=record.name,
+        content=record.content,
+        raw=record.raw,
+        job_id=job_id,
+        step_id=step_id,
+        outcome_id=outcome_id,

+"""MCP client connector that ingests tools and resources from an external server."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import re
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from typing import Any
+
+from fastmcp import Client, FastMCP
+from fastmcp.client.transports import StreamableHttpTransport
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import (
+    HealthStatus,
+    IngestBatch,
+    IngestRecord,
+    McpConnectorSettings,
+)
+from agentic_odi_connectors.protocol import Connector
+
+_ENV_VAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")
+
+
+class MissingEnvironmentError(RuntimeError):
+    """Raised when a connector needs credentials that are not in the environment."""
+
+    def __init__(self, names: list[str]) -> None:
+        self.names = names
+        super().__init__("Missing environment variable(s): " + ", ".join(names))
+
+
+def _expand_env(value: str, environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
+    return _ENV_VAR_PATTERN.sub(lambda match: environ.get(match.group(1), ""), value)
+
+
+def _to_dict(obj: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if hasattr(obj, "model_dump"):
+        dumped = obj.model_dump(mode="json")
+        if isinstance(dumped, dict):
+            return dumped
+    return {"repr": repr(obj)}
+
+
+def _content_text(obj: Any) -> str:
+    parts: list[str] = []
+    content = getattr(obj, "content", None)
+    if content is None:
+        text = getattr(obj, "text", None)
+        return text if isinstance(text, str) else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))
+    for item in content:
+        text = getattr(item, "text", None)
+        if isinstance(text, str):
+            parts.append(text)
+    return "\n".join(parts) if parts else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))
+
+
+class MCPClientConnector(Connector):
+    """Pulls catalog, resources, and optional tool results from an MCP server."""
+
+    kind = "mcp"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        name: str,
+        settings: McpConnectorSettings,
+        *,
+        server: FastMCP | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        self.settings = settings
+        self._server = server
+
+    def transport(self) -> StreamableHttpTransport | FastMCP:
+        """Build the MCP transport, resolving credentials from the environment."""
+        if self._server is not None:
+            return self._server
+        missing = sorted(name for name in self.settings.env_vars if not os.environ.get(name))
+        if missing:
+            raise MissingEnvironmentError(missing)
+        headers = {
+            key: _expand_env(value, os.environ) for key, value in self.settings.headers.items()
+        }
+        return StreamableHttpTransport(
+            url=_expand_env(self.settings.url, os.environ),
+            headers=headers or None,
+            auth="oauth" if self.settings.auth == "oauth" else None,
+        )
+
+    def _client(self) -> Client:
+        return Client(self.transport())
+
+    async def health(self) -> HealthStatus:
+        try:
+            async with self._client() as client:
+                tools = await client.list_tools()
+                resources = await client.list_resources()
+            return HealthStatus(
+                ok=True,
+                message="reachable",
+                details={
+                    "tool_count": len(tools),
+                    "resource_count": len(resources),
+                },
+            )
+        except MissingEnvironmentError as exc:
+            return HealthStatus(
+                ok=False,
+                message=str(exc),
+                details={"missing_env": exc.names},
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            return HealthStatus(ok=False, message=str(exc))
+
+    async def ingest(self) -> IngestBatch:
+        batch = IngestBatch(connector_name=self.name)
+        try:
+            async with self._client() as client:
+                tools = await client.list_tools()
+                resources = await client.list_resources()
+                tool_dicts = [_to_dict(tool) for tool in tools]
+                resource_dicts = [_to_dict(resource) for resource in resources]
+                catalog_raw = {"tools": tool_dicts, "resources": resource_dicts}
+                batch.records.append(
+                    IngestRecord(
+                        source_name=self.name,
+                        source_kind=self.kind,
+                        item_type="catalog",
+                        name="mcp-catalog",
+                        content=json.dumps(catalog_raw, indent=2),
+                        raw=catalog_raw,
+                    )
+                )
+                for resource in resources:
+                    uri = str(getattr(resource, "uri", ""))
+                    name = str(getattr(resource, "name", None) or uri)
+                    try:
+                        contents = await client.read_resource(uri)
+                        content_text = "\n".join(
+                            getattr(item, "text", "") or "" for item in contents
+                        )
+                        batch.records.append(
+                            IngestRecord(
+                                source_name=self.name,
+                                source_kind=self.kind,
+                                item_type="resource",
+                                name=name,
+                                content=content_text,
+                                raw={"uri": uri, "resource": _to_dict(resource)},
+                            )
+                        )
+                    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Failed to read resource {uri}: {exc}")
+                configured_tools = self.settings.tools
+                available = {str(getattr(tool, "name", "")) for tool in tools}
+                for tool_name in configured_tools:
+                    if tool_name not in available:
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Tool not found: {tool_name}")
+                        continue
+                    try:
+                        result = await client.call_tool(tool_name, {})
+                        batch.records.append(
+                            IngestRecord(
+                                source_name=self.name,
+                                source_kind=self.kind,
+                                item_type="tool_result",
+                                name=tool_name,
+                                content=_content_text(result),
+                                raw={"tool": tool_name, "result": _to_dict(result)},
+                            )
+                        )
+                    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Failed to call tool {tool_name}: {exc}")
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            batch.errors.append(str(exc))
+        return batch

+"""Resolve the shared connector configuration file path.
+
+The path is shared by the CLI, the Living Studio sidecar, and the MCP
+ingest connector so every entry point reads and writes the same
+``connectors.json``. An explicit override is honored via the
+``AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`` environment variable; otherwise the
+config lives under the user's platform config directory.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+
+CONFIG_PATH_ENV = "AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG"
+
+
+def config_path() -> Path:
+    """Return the path to the shared ``connectors.json`` registry file."""
+    env = os.getenv(CONFIG_PATH_ENV)
+    if env:
+        return Path(env)
+    return Path.home() / ".config" / "agentic-odi" / "connectors.json"
+
+
+__all__ = ["CONFIG_PATH_ENV", "config_path"]

+"""JSON-backed registry of named connector configurations."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import ConnectorConfig
+
+
+class UnknownConnectorKindError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, kind: str) -> None:
+        self.kind = kind
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown connector kind: {kind}")
+
+
+class DuplicateConnectorError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        super().__init__(f"Connector already exists: {name}")
+
+
+class ConnectorNotFoundError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        super().__init__(f"Connector not found: {name}")
+
+
+def _known_kinds() -> set[str]:
+    from agentic_odi_connectors.factory import known_kinds
+
+    return known_kinds()
+
+
+class ConnectorRegistry:
+    """Persists connector configs to a JSON file."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
+        self.path = path
+
+    def add(self, config: ConnectorConfig) -> None:
+        if config.kind not in _known_kinds():
+            raise UnknownConnectorKindError(config.kind)
+        connectors = self._load()
+        if any(existing.name == config.name for existing in connectors):
+            raise DuplicateConnectorError(config.name)
+        connectors.append(config)
+        self._save(connectors)
+
+    def list_all(self) -> list[ConnectorConfig]:
+        return self._load()
+
+    def get(self, name: str) -> ConnectorConfig:
+        for config in self._load():
+            if config.name == name:
+                return config
+        raise ConnectorNotFoundError(name)
+
+    def delete(self, name: str) -> bool:
+        connectors = self._load()
+        kept = [config for config in connectors if config.name != name]
+        if len(kept) == len(connectors):
+            raise ConnectorNotFoundError(name)
+        self._save(kept)
+        return True
+
+    def _load(self) -> list[ConnectorConfig]:
+        if not self.path.exists():
+            return []
+        with self.path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            payload: dict[str, Any] = json.load(handle)
+        raw_connectors = payload.get("connectors", [])
+        return [ConnectorConfig.model_validate(item) for item in raw_connectors]
+
+    def _save(self, connectors: list[ConnectorConfig]) -> None:
+        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        payload = {"connectors": [item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in connectors]}
+        with self.path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2)
+            handle.write("\n")

+"""REST and webhook connector kinds.
+
+Both kinds share one HTTP puller: a REST endpoint returns a JSON document, and a
+webhook connector posts a configured request (usually to a webhook inbox or a
+subscription endpoint) and normalizes the JSON response. The transport is
+injectable so tests never touch the network.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import urllib.request
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from typing import Any
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import (
+    HealthStatus,
+    IngestBatch,
+    IngestRecord,
+    RestConnectorSettings,
+)
+from agentic_odi_connectors.protocol import Connector
+
+FetchResult = tuple[int, bytes]
+Fetcher = Callable[[str, str, dict[str, str], bytes | None, float], FetchResult]
+
+
+def _default_fetch(
+    method: str,
+    url: str,
+    headers: dict[str, str],
+    body: bytes | None,
+    timeout: float,
+) -> FetchResult:
+    request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, headers=headers, method=method)
+    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:  # nosec B310
+        return int(response.status), response.read()
+
+
+def _lookup(payload: Any, path: str) -> Any:
+    current = payload
+    for part in path.split("."):
+        if not isinstance(current, dict) or part not in current:
+            return None
+        current = current[part]
+    return current
+
+
+class RestConnector(Connector):
+    """Pulls JSON records from an HTTP endpoint into the ingest sink."""
+
+    kind = "rest"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        name: str,
+        settings: RestConnectorSettings,
+        *,
+        kind: str | None = None,
+        fetcher: Fetcher | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        self.settings = settings
+        self.kind = kind or type(self).kind
+        self._fetch = fetcher or _default_fetch
+
+    def _request(self) -> FetchResult:
+        body = None
+        headers = dict(self.settings.headers)
+        if self.settings.json_body is not None:
+            body = json.dumps(self.settings.json_body).encode("utf-8")
+            headers.setdefault("Content-Type", "application/json")
+        return self._fetch(
+            self.settings.method,
+            self.settings.url,
+            headers,
+            body,
+            self.settings.timeout,
+        )
+
+    def _items(self, payload: Any) -> list[Any]:
+        if self.settings.records_key:
+            extracted = _lookup(payload, self.settings.records_key)
+            if isinstance(extracted, list):
+                return extracted
+        if isinstance(payload, list):
+            return payload
+        if isinstance(payload, dict):
+            for key in ("records", "items", "data"):
+                value = payload.get(key)
+                if isinstance(value, list):
+                    return value
+        return [payload]
+
+    def _record(self, item: Any, index: int) -> IngestRecord:
+        if isinstance(item, dict):
+            name = str(
+                item.get("name")
+                or item.get("title")
+                or item.get("id")
+                or f"{self.name}-{index + 1}"
+            )
+            content = None
+            for key in ("content", "text", "description", "body", "summary"):
+                if isinstance(item.get(key), str):
+                    content = item[key]
+                    break
+            if content is None:
+                content = json.dumps(item, indent=2, default=str)
+            raw = item
+        elif isinstance(item, str):
+            name = f"{self.name}-{index + 1}"
+            content = item
+            raw = {"value": item}
+        else:
+            name = f"{self.name}-{index + 1}"
+            content = json.dumps(item, default=str)
+            raw = {"value": item}
+        return IngestRecord(
+            source_name=self.name,
+            source_kind=self.kind,
+            item_type=self.settings.item_type,
+            name=name,
+            content=content,
+            raw=raw,
+        )
+
+    async def health(self) -> HealthStatus:
+        try:
+            status, _ = self._request()
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            return HealthStatus(ok=False, message=str(exc))
+        ok = 200 <= status < 400
+        return HealthStatus(
+            ok=ok,
+            message="reachable" if ok else f"HTTP {status}",
+            details={"status": status, "url": self.settings.url},
+        )
+
+    async def ingest(self) -> IngestBatch:
+        batch = IngestBatch(connector_name=self.name)
+        try:
+            status, body = self._request()
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            batch.errors.append(str(exc))
+            return batch
+        if not 200 <= status < 400:
+            batch.errors.append(f"HTTP {status} from {self.settings.url}")
+            return batch
+        text = body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+        try:
+            payload: Any = json.loads(text)
+        except json.JSONDecodeError:
+            payload = text
+        records = self._items(payload)
+        for index, item in enumerate(records):
+            batch.records.append(self._record(item, index))
+        return batch
+
+
+class WebhookConnector(RestConnector):
+    """Posts to a webhook endpoint and ingests the JSON response."""
+
+    kind = "webhook"

+class IngestSink:

+from agentic_odi_connectors.rest.connector import RestConnector, WebhookConnector
+
+Calls = list[tuple[str, str, dict[str, str], bytes | None, float]]
+
+
+def _fetcher(status: int, payload: Any, calls: Calls | None = None):
+    def fetch(
+        method: str, url: str, headers: dict[str, str], body: bytes | None, timeout: float
+    ) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
+        if calls is not None:
+            calls.append((method, url, headers, body, timeout))
+        text = payload if isinstance(payload, str) else json.dumps(payload)
+        return status, text.encode("utf-8")
+
+    return fetch
+
+
+def _connector(payload: Any, status: int = 200, **settings: Any) -> RestConnector:
+    base: dict[str, Any] = {"url": "https://api.example/records"}
+    base.update(settings)
+    return RestConnector(
+        name="jira",
+        settings=RestConnectorSettings(**base),
+        fetcher=_fetcher(status, payload),
+    )
+

@@ -0,0 +1,64 @@
+"""Evaluate desired-outcome statements against the ODI format."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+_CONTEXT_MARKERS = (
+    " when ",
+    " while ",
+    " before ",
+    " after ",
+    " during ",
+    " if ",
+    " as ",
+)
+
+_VAGUE_TERMS = ("better", "improve", "optimize", "faster", "easier")
+
+
+def evaluate_outcome_statement(statement: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Return format feedback for a desired-outcome statement."""
+    text = statement.strip()
+    lowered = text.lower()
+    padded = f" {lowered} "
+    issues: list[str] = []
+    suggestions: list[str] = []
+
+    direction: str | None = None
+    if lowered.startswith("minimize"):
+        direction = "minimize"
+    elif lowered.startswith("maximize"):
+        direction = "maximize"
+    else:
+        issues.append("Statement must start with 'Minimize' or 'Maximize'.")
+        suggestions.append("Start with 'Minimize/Maximize the [metric] ...'.")
+
+    if " the " not in padded:
+        issues.append("Name the object of control after 'the'.")
+        suggestions.append("Say what is being minimized or maximized, e.g. 'the time to ...'.")
+
+    if not any(marker in padded for marker in _CONTEXT_MARKERS):
+        issues.append("Add the execution context with 'when ...', 'while ...', or 'before ...'.")
+        suggestions.append("Close with the situation, e.g. '... when onboarding a new customer'.")
+
+    if len(text.split()) < 4:
+        issues.append("Statement is too short to describe a measurable outcome.")
+        suggestions.append("Describe the metric, the object, and the context.")
+
+    if len(text) > 200:
+        issues.append("Statement is longer than 200 characters; keep it to one measurable outcome.")
+        suggestions.append("Split broad statements into separate outcomes.")
+
+    vague = [term for term in _VAGUE_TERMS if term in lowered]
+    if vague:
+        issues.append(f"Replace vague terms with a measurable metric: {', '.join(vague)}.")
+        suggestions.append("Use a metric such as time, cost, effort, errors, or likelihood.")
+
+    return {
+        "statement": text,
+        "valid": not issues,
+        "direction": direction,
+        "issues": issues,
+        "suggestions": suggestions,
+    }

@@ -0,0 +1,99 @@
+"""Event-store contract shared by local SQLite and cloud adapters."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import uuid
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Protocol, TypedDict
+
+DEFAULT_WORKSPACE = "local"
+DEFAULT_DEVICE = "local"
+
+
+class Event(TypedDict):
+    """A single append-only domain event."""
+
+    id: int
+    event_id: str
+    workspace_id: str
+    device_id: str
+    timestamp: str
+    type: str
+    payload: dict[str, Any]
+    server_seq: int | None
+
+
+class EventStore(Protocol):
+    """Persistence boundary for the append-only event log."""
+
+    def append(
+        self,
+        event_type: str,
+        payload: dict[str, Any],
+        *,
+        event_id: str | None = None,
+        workspace_id: str = DEFAULT_WORKSPACE,
+        device_id: str = DEFAULT_DEVICE,
+    ) -> Event: ...
+
+    def get_stream(
+        self,
+        *,
+        workspace_id: str | None = None,
+        after_server_seq: int = 0,
+        unsynced_only: bool = False,
+        replay_order: bool = False,
+    ) -> list[Event]: ...
+
+    def insert_remote(self, events: list[Event]) -> int: ...
+
+    def mark_synced(self, server_seqs: dict[str, int]) -> int: ...
+
+    def retag_workspace(self, old: str, new: str) -> int: ...
+
+    def max_server_seq(self, workspace_id: str) -> int: ...
+
+    def get_cursor(self, workspace_id: str) -> int: ...
+
+    def set_cursor(self, workspace_id: str, remote_url: str, seq: int) -> None: ...
+
+    def pending_count(self, workspace_id: str) -> int: ...
+
+    def clear(self, *, workspace_id: str | None = None) -> None: ...
+
+    def close(self) -> None: ...
+
+
+def new_event_id() -> str:
+    """Return a globally unique, client-generated event identifier."""
+    return uuid.uuid4().hex
+
+
+def default_device_path() -> Path:
+    return Path(os.path.expanduser("~/.agentic-odi/device_id"))
+
+
+def resolve_device_id(path: Path | None = None) -> str:
+    """Return a stable random device id, creating it on first use.
+
+    The id is deliberately random: it must not reveal a hostname, user, or
+    anything else about the device.
+    """
+    configured = os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_DEVICE_ID")
+    if configured:
+        return configured
+
+    device_path = path or default_device_path()
+    try:
+        existing = device_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
+    except FileNotFoundError:
+        existing = ""
+
+    if existing:
+        return existing
+
+    device_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    device_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
+    device_path.write_text(device_id + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    return device_id

+"""Repository factory selecting a persistent or in-memory store."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+
+from agentic_odi_core.repository import InMemoryRepository, Repository
+from agentic_odi_core.sqlite_repository import SQLiteRepository
+
+
+def build_repository(db_path: str | None = None) -> Repository:
+    resolved: str | None
+    if db_path is not None:
+        resolved = db_path
+    else:
+        resolved = os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_DB")
+    if resolved is None:
+        resolved = os.path.expanduser("~/.agentic-odi/odi.db")
+    if resolved == ":memory:":
+        return InMemoryRepository()
+    parent = os.path.dirname(resolved)
+    if parent:
+        os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
+    return SQLiteRepository(db_path=resolved)

--- packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/intent_store.py	
+++ packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/intent_store.py	
@@ -0,0 +1,279 @@
+"""Append-only event store backed by SQLite."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import sqlite3
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from typing import Any
+
+from agentic_odi_core.events import (
+    DEFAULT_DEVICE,
+    DEFAULT_WORKSPACE,
+    Event,
+    new_event_id,
+)
+
+_COLUMNS = {
+    "event_id": "TEXT",
+    "workspace_id": "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local'",
+    "device_id": "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local'",
+    "server_seq": "INTEGER",
+}
+
+
+class IntentStore:
+    """SQLite implementation of the append-only event contract."""
+
+    def __init__(self, db_path: str = "intent_store.db", check_same_thread: bool = True) -> None:
+        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, check_same_thread=check_same_thread)
+        self.conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;")
+        self._init_db()
+
+    def _init_db(self) -> None:
+        with self.conn:
+            self.conn.execute(
+                """
+                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
+                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
+                    event_id TEXT,
+                    workspace_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local',
+                    device_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local',
+                    timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    payload TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    server_seq INTEGER
+                )
+                """
+            )
+            self._migrate_events_table()
+            self.conn.execute(
+                "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_event_id ON events(event_id)"
+            )
+            self.conn.execute(
+                """
+                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_workspace_server
+                ON events(workspace_id, server_seq)
+                """
+            )
+            self.conn.execute(
+                """
+                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sync_state (
+                    workspace_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+                    remote_url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+                    last_server_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+                    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
+                )
+                """
+            )
+
+    def _migrate_events_table(self) -> None:
+        existing = {row[1] for row in self.conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(events)").fetchall()}
+        for column, definition in _COLUMNS.items():
+            if column not in existing:
+                self.conn.execute(f"ALTER TABLE events ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}")
+
+        missing_ids = [
+            row[0]
+            for row in self.conn.execute(
+                "SELECT id FROM events WHERE event_id IS NULL OR event_id = ''"
+            ).fetchall()
+        ]
+        for row_id in missing_ids:
+            self.conn.execute(
+                "UPDATE events SET event_id = ? WHERE id = ?",
+                (new_event_id(), row_id),
+            )
+
+    def append(
+        self,
+        event_type: str,
+        payload: dict[str, Any],
+        *,
+        event_id: str | None = None,
+        workspace_id: str = DEFAULT_WORKSPACE,
+        device_id: str = DEFAULT_DEVICE,
+    ) -> Event:
+        resolved_id = event_id or new_event_id()
+        timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
+        payload_json = json.dumps(payload)
+        with self.conn:
+            self.conn.execute(
+                """
+                INSERT OR IGNORE INTO events
+                    (event_id, workspace_id, device_id, timestamp, event_type, payload)
+                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
+                """,
+                (resolved_id, workspace_id, device_id, timestamp, event_type, payload_json),
+            )
+            row = self.conn.execute(
+                """
+                SELECT id, event_id, workspace_id, device_id, timestamp,
+                       event_type, payload, server_seq
+                FROM events WHERE event_id = ?
+                """,
+                (resolved_id,),
+            ).fetchone()
+
+        if row is None:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"event {resolved_id} could not be stored")
+        if row[2] != workspace_id:
+            raise ValueError(f"event_id {resolved_id} already belongs to another workspace")
+        return self._to_event(row)
+
+    def get_stream(
+        self,
+        *,
+        workspace_id: str | None = None,
+        after_server_seq: int = 0,
+        unsynced_only: bool = False,
+        replay_order: bool = False,
+    ) -> list[Event]:
+        clauses: list[str] = []
+        params: list[Any] = []
+        if workspace_id is not None:
+            clauses.append("workspace_id = ?")
+            params.append(workspace_id)
+        if after_server_seq:
+            clauses.append("server_seq IS NOT NULL AND server_seq > ?")
+            params.append(after_server_seq)
+        if unsynced_only:
+            clauses.append("server_seq IS NULL")
+
+        where = f"WHERE {' AND '.join(clauses)}" if clauses else ""
+        if replay_order:
+            order = "ORDER BY (server_seq IS NULL) ASC, server_seq ASC, id ASC"
+        else:
+            order = "ORDER BY id ASC"
+
+        cursor = self.conn.cursor()
+        # `where` and `order` are assembled from the literal fragments above, so
+        # interpolating them cannot inject SQL; every caller value is bound.
+        sql = (
+            "SELECT id, event_id, workspace_id, device_id, timestamp, "
+            "event_type, payload, server_seq FROM events "
+            f"{where} {order}"  # nosec B608 - static fragments, bound values
+        )
+        cursor.execute(sql, params)
+        return [self._to_event(row) for row in cursor.fetchall()]
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _to_event(row: tuple[Any, ...]) -> Event:
+        return Event(
+            id=row[0],
+            event_id=row[1],
+            workspace_id=row[2],
+            device_id=row[3],
+            timestamp=row[4],
+            type=row[5],
+            payload=json.loads(row[6]) if row[6] else {},
+            server_seq=row[7],
+        )
+
+    def insert_remote(self, events: list[Event]) -> int:
+        inserted = 0
+        with self.conn:
+            for event in events:
+                self.conn.execute(
+                    """
+                    INSERT OR IGNORE INTO events
+                        (event_id, workspace_id, device_id, timestamp,
+                         event_type, payload, server_seq)
+                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
+                    """,
+                    (
+                        event["event_id"],
+                        event["workspace_id"],
+                        event["device_id"],
+                        event["timestamp"],
+                        event["type"],
+                        json.dumps(event["payload"]),
+                        event.get("server_seq"),
+                    ),
+                )
+                self.conn.execute(
+                    """
+                    UPDATE events SET server_seq = ?
+                    WHERE event_id = ? AND server_seq IS NULL AND workspace_id = ?
+                    """,
+                    (
+                        event.get("server_seq"),
+                        event["event_id"],
+                        event["workspace_id"],
+                    ),
+                )
+                inserted += 1
+        return inserted
+
+    def mark_synced(self, server_seqs: dict[str, int]) -> int:
+        updated = 0
+        with self.conn:
+            for event_id, server_seq in server_seqs.items():
+                cursor = self.conn.execute(
+                    "UPDATE events SET server_seq = ? WHERE event_id = ? AND server_seq IS NULL",
+                    (server_seq, event_id),
+                )
+                updated += cursor.rowcount
+        return updated
+
+    def retag_workspace(self, old: str, new: str) -> int:
+        updated = 0
+        with self.conn:
+            cursor = self.conn.execute(
+                "UPDATE events SET workspace_id = ? WHERE workspace_id = ?",
+                (new, old),
+            )
+            updated = cursor.rowcount
+            self.conn.execute(
+                "DELETE FROM sync_state WHERE workspace_id = ?",
+                (old,),
+            )
+        return updated
+
+    def max_server_seq(self, workspace_id: str) -> int:
+        row = self.conn.execute(
+            "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(server_seq), 0) FROM events WHERE workspace_id = ?",
+            (workspace_id,),
+        ).fetchone()
+        return int(row[0]) if row else 0
+
+    def get_cursor(self, workspace_id: str) -> int:
+        row = self.conn.execute(
+            "SELECT last_server_seq FROM sync_state WHERE workspace_id = ?",
+            (workspace_id,),
+        ).fetchone()
+        return int(row[0]) if row else 0
+
+    def set_cursor(self, workspace_id: str, remote_url: str, seq: int) -> None:
+        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
+        with self.conn:
+            self.conn.execute(
+                """
+                INSERT INTO sync_state (workspace_id, remote_url, last_server_seq, updated_at)
+                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
+                ON CONFLICT(workspace_id) DO UPDATE SET
+                    remote_url = excluded.remote_url,
+                    last_server_seq = excluded.last_server_seq,
+                    updated_at = excluded.updated_at
+                """,
+                (workspace_id, remote_url, seq, now),
+            )
+
+    def pending_count(self, workspace_id: str) -> int:
+        row = self.conn.execute(
+            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE workspace_id = ? AND server_seq IS NULL",
+            (workspace_id,),
+        ).fetchone()
+        return int(row[0]) if row else 0
+
+    def clear(self, *, workspace_id: str | None = None) -> None:
+        with self.conn:
+            if workspace_id is None:
+                self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM events")
+                self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM sync_state")
+            else:
+                self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM events WHERE workspace_id = ?", (workspace_id,))
+                self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM sync_state WHERE workspace_id = ?", (workspace_id,))
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.conn.close()

+ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT = """You are an expert in Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI). Your purpose is to help users discover, define, and prioritize high-value jobs, desired outcomes, and opportunities."""

+ODI_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES = """## Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) — Stage-by-Stage Tool Guide
+
+Follow this sequence when guiding a user through the ODI process:
+
+### Stage 1: Define Intent (Job-to-be-Done)
+- **When**: Always start here if no Job exists.
+- **Ask the user**: 'What is the main task or goal your customer is trying to accomplish?'
+- **Tools to use**:
+  - `add_job(name, description)` — Create the Job once identified.
+  - `get_jobs()` — Check if a relevant Job already exists before creating a new one.
+  - `get_job(job_id)` — Retrieve details of a specific existing Job.
+
+### Stage 2: Capture Desired Outcomes
+- **When**: After a Job is defined. Outcomes come BEFORE steps or solutions.
+- **Ask the user**: 'What does success look like? What should happen faster, more reliably, or more consistently?'
+- **Outcome statement format**: 'Minimize/Maximize the [metric] when [context].'
+- **Tools to use**:
+  - `add_outcome(job_id, statement, importance, satisfaction)` — Capture each desired outcome with scores.
+  - `get_outcomes(job_id)` — Review all outcomes captured for a Job.
+  - `evaluate_outcome(statement, job_id?)` — Check that a statement starts with Minimize/Maximize, names a metric, and states its context before saving it.
+
+### Stage 3: Calculate Opportunity Scores
+- **When**: After outcomes have importance and satisfaction scores.
+- **Formula**: Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)
+- **Scores > 10** indicate high innovation opportunity. Guide the user to focus efforts there.
+- **Tools to use**: `get_outcomes(job_id)` — Review opportunity_score field on each outcome.
+
+### Stage 4: Build the Job Map
+- **When**: After key outcomes are captured. Use to organize the job execution context.
+- **Ask the user**: 'What are the key phases or steps the customer takes when doing this job?'
+- **Tools to use**:
+  - `add_step(job_id, name, order)` — Add each chronological step.
+  - `get_job_map(job_id)` — View the complete ordered job map.
+
+### Supporting Tools
+- `add_evidence(...)` / `list_evidence(job_id?)` — Attach customer research records from connectors to a Job, Step, or Outcome without altering the ODI artifacts.
+- `promote_evidence(evidence_id, target, job_id?)` — Turn a captured record into a Job or desired Outcome when it is ready.
+- `get_odi_schema()` — Return the canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity.
+
+### General Rule
+Never skip stages. Always confirm the user has a Job defined (Stage 1) before capturing Outcomes (Stage 2), and always capture Outcomes (Stage 2) before building the Job Map (Stage 4)."""

+"""Core domain models for Agentic ODI."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import uuid
+from enum import Enum
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, computed_field
+
+
+class Direction(str, Enum):
+    MINIMIZE = "minimize"
+    MAXIMIZE = "maximize"
+
+
+class BusinessImpactCategory(str, Enum):
+    REVENUE_GROWTH = "revenue_growth"
+    COST_REDUCTION = "cost_reduction"
+    RETENTION = "retention"
+    RISK_MITIGATION = "risk_mitigation"
+    OPERATIONAL_EFFICIENCY = "operational_efficiency"
+    COMPLIANCE = "compliance"
+    BRAND_REPUTATION = "brand_reputation"
+    OTHER = "other"
+
+
+def compute_opportunity_score(importance: float, satisfaction: float) -> float:
+    """ODI Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)."""
+    return float(importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0.0))
+
+
+class Job(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the Job-to-be-Done")
+    description: str | None = Field(None, description="Detailed description of the Job")
+
+
+class Step(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this step belongs to")
+    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the job step")
+    order: int = Field(..., description="The chronological order of this step in the job map")
+
+
+class Outcome(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
+    step_id: str | None = Field(None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable")
+    statement: str = Field(
+        ..., description="The desired outcome statement (e.g., 'Minimize the time it takes to...')"
+    )
+    importance: float | None = Field(None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Importance score (1-10)")
+    satisfaction: float | None = Field(
+        None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Current satisfaction score (1-10)"
+    )
+    opportunity_score: float | None = Field(
+        None, description="Opportunity score (Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0))"
+    )
+
+
+class ValueMetric(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    direction: Direction
+    unit_of_measure: str
+    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+
+    @computed_field
+    @property
+    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
+        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)
+
+
+class CustomerValue(BaseModel):
+    direction: Direction
+    unit_of_measure: str
+    object_of_control: str
+    contextual_clarifier: str | None = None
+    statement: str
+    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+    value_metrics: list[ValueMetric] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+    @computed_field
+    @property
+    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
+        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)
+
+
+class BusinessValue(BaseModel):
+    category: BusinessImpactCategory
+    statement: str
+    detail: str | None = None
+    estimated_annual_value: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0)
+    confidence: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
+
+
+EvidenceItemType = Literal["catalog", "resource", "tool_result", "manual", "note"]
+
+
+class Evidence(BaseModel):
+    """A captured research record linked (optionally) to ODI artifacts."""
+
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    source_name: str = Field(..., description="Connector or person that produced the record")
+    source_kind: str = Field(..., description="Connector kind, e.g. mcp, rest, webhook, manual")
+    item_type: EvidenceItemType = Field(
+        "manual", description="Normalized record kind produced by the connector"
+    )
+    name: str = Field(..., description="Short human-readable label for the record")
+    content: str = Field(..., description="Normalized text content of the record")
+    raw: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict, description="Original record payload")
+    job_id: str | None = Field(None, description="Job this evidence supports")
+    step_id: str | None = Field(None, description="Job-map Step this evidence supports")
+    outcome_id: str | None = Field(None, description="Desired Outcome this evidence supports")
+
+
+class CustomerOutcome(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
+    step_id: str | None = Field(
+        default=None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable"
+    )
+    customer_value: CustomerValue
+    business_value: BusinessValue
+
+    @computed_field
+    @property
+    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
+        return self.customer_value.opportunity_score

+"""Repository interfaces and in-memory implementation."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Protocol
+
+from agentic_odi_core.models import CustomerOutcome, Evidence, Job, Outcome, Step
+
+
+class Repository(Protocol):
+    jobs: dict[str, Job]
+    steps: dict[str, Step]
+    outcomes: dict[str, Outcome]
+    customer_outcomes: dict[str, CustomerOutcome]
+    evidence: dict[str, Evidence]
+
+    def add_job(self, job: Job) -> Job: ...
+    def list_jobs(self) -> list[Job]: ...
+    def get_job(self, job_id: str) -> Job | None: ...
+    def update_job(self, job_id: str, updates: dict) -> Job | None: ...
+    def delete_job(self, job_id: str) -> bool: ...
+    def add_step(self, step: Step) -> Step: ...
+    def get_step(self, step_id: str) -> Step | None: ...
+    def get_steps_for_job(self, job_id: str) -> list[Step]: ...
+    def update_step(self, step_id: str, updates: dict) -> Step | None: ...
+    def delete_step(self, step_id: str) -> bool: ...
+    def add_outcome(self, outcome: Outcome) -> Outcome: ...
+    def get_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> Outcome | None: ...
+    def get_outcomes(self, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> list[Outcome]: ...
+    def update_outcome(self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict) -> Outcome | None: ...
+    def delete_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> bool: ...
+    def add_customer_outcome(self, co: CustomerOutcome) -> CustomerOutcome: ...
+    def get_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> CustomerOutcome | None: ...
+    def list_customer_outcomes(self, job_id: str | None = None) -> list[CustomerOutcome]: ...
+    def update_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict) -> CustomerOutcome | None: ...
+    def delete_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> bool: ...
+    def add_evidence(self, evidence: Evidence) -> Evidence: ...
+    def get_evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> Evidence | None: ...
+    def list_evidence(
+        self,
+        job_id: str | None = None,
+        step_id: str | None = None,
+        outcome_id: str | None = None,
+    ) -> list[Evidence]: ...
+    def delete_evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> bool: ...
+    def clear(self) -> None: ...
+
+
+class InMemoryRepository:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.jobs: dict[str, Job] = {}
+        self.steps: dict[str, Step] = {}
+        self.outcomes: dict[str, Outcome] = {}
+        self.customer_outcomes: dict[str, CustomerOutcome] = {}
+        self.evidence: dict[str, Evidence] = {}
+
+    def add_job(self, job: Job) -> Job:
+        self.jobs[job.id] = job
+        return job
+
+    def list_jobs(self) -> list[Job]:
+        return list(self.jobs.values())
+
+    def get_job(self, job_id: str) -> Job | None:
+        return self.jobs.get(job_id)
+
+    def update_job(self, job_id: str, updates: dict) -> Job | None:
+        job = self.jobs.get(job_id)
+        if not job:
+            return None
+        current = job.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
+        current.update(updates)
+        new_job = job.model_validate(current)
+        self.jobs[job_id] = new_job
+        return new_job
+
+    def delete_job(self, job_id: str) -> bool:
+        if job_id not in self.jobs:
+            return False
+        del self.jobs[job_id]
+        for key in [k for k, v in self.steps.items() if v.job_id == job_id]:
+            del self.steps[key]
+        for key in [k for k, v in self.outcomes.items() if v.job_id == job_id]:
+            del self.outcomes[key]
+        for key in [k for k, v in self.customer_outcomes.items() if v.job_id == job_id]:
+            del self.customer_outcomes[key]
+        for key in [
+            k
+            for k, v in self.evidence.items()
+            if v.job_id == job_id
+            or (v.step_id is not None and v.step_id not in self.steps)
+            or (v.outcome_id is not None and v.outcome_id not in self.outcomes)
+        ]:
+            del self.evidence[key]
+        return True
+
+    def add_step(self, step: Step) -> Step:
+        self.steps[step.id] = step
+        return step
+
+    def get_step(self, step_id: str) -> Step | None:
+        return self.steps.get(step_id)
+
+    def get_steps_for_job(self, job_id: str) -> list[Step]:
+        return [s for s in self.steps.values() if s.job_id == job_id]
+
+    def update_step(self, step_id: str, updates: dict) -> Step | None:
+        step = self.steps.get(step_id)
+        if not step:
+            return None
+        current = step.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
+        current.update(updates)
+        new_step = step.model_validate(current)
+        self.steps[step_id] = new_step
+        return new_step
+
+    def delete_step(self, step_id: str) -> bool:
+        if step_id not in self.steps:
+            return False
+        del self.steps[step_id]
+        for key in [k for k, v in self.outcomes.items() if v.step_id == step_id]:
+            del self.outcomes[key]
+        for key in [k for k, v in self.customer_outcomes.items() if v.step_id == step_id]:
+            del self.customer_outcomes[key]
+        for key in [
+            k
+            for k, v in self.evidence.items()
+            if v.step_id == step_id
+            or (v.outcome_id is not None and v.outcome_id not in self.outcomes)
+        ]:
+            del self.evidence[key]
+        return True
+
+    def add_outcome(self, outcome: Outcome) -> Outcome:
+        self.outcomes[outcome.id] = outcome
+        return outcome
+
+    def get_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> Outcome | None:
+        return self.outcomes.get(outcome_id)
+
+    def get_outcomes(self, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> list[Outcome]:
+        outs = [o for o in self.outcomes.values() if o.job_id == job_id]
+        if step_id is not None:
+            outs = [o for o in outs if o.step_id == step_id]
+        return outs
+
+    def update_outcome(self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict) -> Outcome | None:
+        outcome = self.outcomes.get(outcome_id)
+        if not outcome:
+            return None
+        current = outcome.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
+        current.update(updates)
+        new_outcome = outcome.model_validate(current)
+        self.outcomes[outcome_id] = new_outcome
+        return new_outcome
+
+    def delete_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> bool:
+        if outcome_id in self.outcomes:
+            del self.outcomes[outcome_id]
+            for key in [k for k, v in self.evidence.items() if v.outcome_id == outcome_id]:
+                del self.evidence[key]

+        return False
+
+    def add_customer_outcome(self, co: CustomerOutcome) -> CustomerOutcome:
+        self.customer_outcomes[co.id] = co
+        return co
+
+    def get_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> CustomerOutcome | None:
+        return self.customer_outcomes.get(outcome_id)
+
+    def list_customer_outcomes(self, job_id: str | None = None) -> list[CustomerOutcome]:
+        if job_id is None:
+            return list(self.customer_outcomes.values())

+    def update_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict) -> CustomerOutcome | None:

+    def delete_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> bool:
+        if outcome_id in self.customer_outcomes:
+            del self.customer_outcomes[outcome_id]
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    def add_evidence(self, evidence: Evidence) -> Evidence:
+        self.evidence[evidence.id] = evidence
+        return evidence
+
+    def get_evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> Evidence | None:
+        return self.evidence.get(evidence_id)
+
+    def list_evidence(
+        self,
+        job_id: str | None = None,

+    ) -> list[Evidence]:
+        items = list(self.evidence.values())
+        if job_id is not None:
+            items = [item for item in items if item.job_id == job_id]
+        if step_id is not None:
+            items = [item for item in items if item.step_id == step_id]
+        if outcome_id is not None:
+            items = [item for item in items if item.outcome_id == outcome_id]
+        return items
+
+    def delete_evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> bool:
+        if evidence_id in self.evidence:
+            del self.evidence[evidence_id]
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        self.jobs.clear()
+        self.steps.clear()
+        self.outcomes.clear()
+        self.customer_outcomes.clear()
+        self.evidence.clear()

@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+"""Canonical JSON schemas for every ODI entity.
+
+These schemas are the machine-readable contract used by agents, connectors, and
+CLI consumers. They are derived from the Pydantic models so there is exactly one
+definition of the ODI dataset.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+from agentic_odi_core.models import (
+    BusinessValue,
+    CustomerOutcome,
+    CustomerValue,
+    Evidence,
+    Job,
+    Outcome,
+    Step,
+    ValueMetric,
+)
+
+_SCHEMA_MODELS: dict[str, type[BaseModel]] = {
+    "Job": Job,
+    "Step": Step,
+    "Outcome": Outcome,
+    "ValueMetric": ValueMetric,
+    "CustomerValue": CustomerValue,
+    "BusinessValue": BusinessValue,
+    "CustomerOutcome": CustomerOutcome,
+    "Evidence": Evidence,
+}
+
+
+def odi_schema() -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Return the JSON schema for each ODI entity keyed by model name."""
+    return {name: model.model_json_schema() for name, model in _SCHEMA_MODELS.items()}
